newsitem.title: FINLAND: RAISIO SAYS BENECOL SWEDEN PLAN ON TRACK.
newsitem.headline: RAISIO SAYS BENECOL SWEDEN PLAN ON TRACK.

text.p: Finnish food group Raision Tehtaat Oy said on Wednesday its plan to launch its patented cholesterol-cutting margarine Benecol in Sweden this year was still on track, with no reason to expect a setback.

Spokesman Sten von Hellens told Reuters the company had "no reason to expect that we would not get approval" from Swedish health authorities for Benecol, which contains cholesterol- reducing stanol esters, as a special dietary product there.
He was speaking in response to recent volatility in Raisio's share, partly attributed to a Swedish media report which suggested authorities there may hold back on Benecol approval.

That report highlighted Swedish authorities' doubts about medical claims on foodstuffs. Von Hellens said the same concerns apply in Finland, where Benecol is licensed as a special dietary product: no medical claims are made in its marketing.
Von Hellens said Raisio, which expects a surplus supply of the key stanol esters in Benecol at the start of 1998, was also looking at possibilities of launching it in other markets.
He said the company could in theory launch Benecol in any European Union country but had chosen to talk to each country's authorities to seek "special dietary" status for the product.

In line with Raisio's plans to launch Benecol in other countries besides Sweden once its stanol supply is in surplus, Von Hellens said the company was negotiating with other companies, but gave no more details.

Raisio's stock -- prone to volatility after news of the Benecol launch last year drew massive international interest and sharp gains -- has been particularly volatile but thinly traded this week amid various rumours.
Brokers say a large chunk of stock is believed to be up for sale as operators seek to unlock profits.

Raisio, which advanced by well over 400 percent during 1996 but weakened towards year-end to around 290 markka, in March scaled a new year-high of 500 markka but recently fell back through the 400 markka level.
It recovered some ground in late Wednesday trade to 395 markka, up 11.00 markka or nearly three percent.
-- Sara Henley, Helsinki newsroom +3589 6805 0247, e-mail news@reuters.fi
